Optimism relays and Across governance on PulseChain
1 October 2026. All investigation is read-only. This study decodes eight examined transactions,
compares relevant inherited and current state, and connects one proposed governance action to its
previously verified execution. Addresses identify accounts and contracts, not people.
The records establish three different activities: an inherited Synthetix administrative message, later
settlement of inherited Optimism withdrawals, and postfork control changes in Across. They do not
establish that the same account owns every component.
The eight transactions, in chronological order
UTC date Transaction Recorded action Meaning
4 May 2023 fd38…da9 Synthetix Safe calls its
Ethereum owner relay,
which sends an Optimism
instruction to give an
account Futures suspend/
resume permission
A pre-fork Ethereum
governance operation
inherited by PulseChain
24 August 2024 385e…755 Optimism messenger
proves a withdrawal and the
copied standard bridge pays
0.02 native PLS
Successful local settlement
using an April 2023 state
commitment
6 October 2024 38b6…f93 Optimism DAI bridge
releases
301,632.643171596086897
512 local DAI to Across
HubPool
A direct Across/Optimism
settlement connection using
a May 2023 commitment
29 October 2024 3055…383 BAD9 sends 1 PLS to
HubPool's 
loadEthForL2Calls()
Prefunding for future cross-
chain fees; this transaction
contains no L2 call
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 310

UTC date Transaction Recorded action Meaning
14 June 2026 c5e7…7e2 feca proposes transferring
HubPool ownership to itself
through the Across Safe's
OptimisticGovernor module
An UMA assertion-backed
proposal; execution is a
separate transaction
19 June 2026 9abe…56f feca calls HubPool's owner-
only 
emergencyDeleteProposal()
and refunds a 0.45 copied-
WETH bond
Administration of an Across
rebalance bundle after
acquiring ownership
2 July 2026 fae8…61b feca configures an adapter
and spoke for chain ID
88888
Direct evidence of Across
configuration authority; no
message is sent in this
transaction
5 August 2026 4d84…c09 1967 executes Aave
proposal 218, sending its
queued MAI listing
instruction toward Optimism
Permissionless execution of
a queued proposal, with an
outbound L1-to-L2 message
All eight saved receipts report success. The offline decoder checks transaction, receipt, trace and block-
header identities and the transaction's inclusion in its recorded block. Failed optional subcalls in the
native withdrawal are retained; its actual payment succeeds. This is one-provider evidence, with a
separate Ethereum check of the pre-fork Synthetix transaction and inherited proof predicates.
Synthetix has its own cross-chain administrative relay
The first transaction is block 17,187,730, before the inherited boundary 17,232,999. An Ethereum RPC
returns the same transaction and block. Its caller is 0x302d2451d9f47620374b54c521423bf0403916a2, not 1967.
Synthetix Safe on L1
  → OwnerRelayOnEthereum
  → Optimism messenger sends instruction
  → designated OwnerRelayOnOptimism on L2
  → authorized L2 target
The decoded instruction targets SystemStatus 0xe8c41be1a167314abaf2423b72bf8da826943ffd and authorizes 
0x6cd3f878852769e04a723a5f66ca7dd4d9e38a6c to suspend and resume the Futures section. This is a specific
permission, not a universal token-minting grant.
SIP-167 describes this architecture. The preserved, integrity-checked synthetix@2.88.1 source requires the
L1 relay's owner to initiate instructions. The L2 relay requires both the designated messenger as caller
and the correct cross-domain sender. Consequently, effective control of the Synthetix Safe could
administer suitably owned L2 Synthetix contracts without owning the Optimism messenger itself. Current
private-L2 delivery and ownership are not inspected.
At PulseChain block 27,684,339, Synthetix's L1 relay owner remains Safe 
0xeb3107117fead7de89cd14d463d340a2e6917769; its nominee is zero and its resolver cache is valid. The Safe
threshold is five of thirteen. Its sampled isOwner(1967) is false. Signer-key control, an undiscovered
authorization route or private-L2 changes are not resolved by those getters.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 311

The Aave execution does not demonstrate a new vote or messenger
ownership
The August transaction calls execute(218) on Aave Governance V2. Published code permits execution once
the governance and timelock conditions pass. The recorded path is governance → short executor →
message adapter → Optimism sendMessage.
The inner instruction queues payload 0x1720d605289a189c5fbd360ca2307db5c6d3fdfd at Optimism executor 
0x7d9103572be58ffe99dc390e8246f02dcae6f611. Its bytes match the original proposal 218 execution report
retained in the Aave history study (Appendix 2). The destination proposal concerned MAI listing on Aave
V3 Optimism; destination execution on the private source environment is not shown here.
The inherited and current getters return the same 424,248.253753485267005365 votes for and zero
against. Both return zero voting power for 1967 in this proposal. No vote-casting call occurs in the
examined transaction. Its execution flag changes from false at the fork to true at the current checkpoint.
Calls to AddressManager 0xde1fcfb0851916ca5101820a69b13a4e276bd81f are STATICCALL getAddress(string) registry
reads. They do not update ownership or mappings. The registry and messenger report the separate
Optimism Safe 0x9ba6e03d8b90de867373db8cf1a58d2f7f006b3a, threshold five of seven. Its sampled isOwner(1967)
is false. Calling a governance executor or passing through a messenger is different from controlling
either contract.
Old Optimism proofs can settle locally after the fork
The two withdrawal proofs reference state commitments dated 10 April 2023 and 9 May 2023. Calling
the exact recorded verifyStateCommitment view calldata at the Ethereum fork block returns true for both.
The April commitment was already outside the challenge period; the May commitment remained inside it
at the fork and was mature by its October 2024 settlement. Message-success flags change from false at
the inherited comparison to true at the current checkpoint.
The native withdrawal authenticates the L2 standard bridge 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010 and
pays 0x5da70d2a1858a883b42d560edeb5a4ff4e7829fe. A copied ETH balance/payment is native PLS on PulseChain.
Optional failed isUpgrading() probes are tolerated by the published ChugSplashProxy logic; they are not
Safe signer changes.
The DAI withdrawal authenticates L2 DAI bridge 0x467194771dae2967aef3ecbedd3bf9a310c76c65. Source DAI is 
0xda10009cbd5d07dd0cecc66161fc93d7c9000da1; destination DAI is the existing local 
0x6b175474e89094c44da98b954eedeac495271d0f. The source user is Across's Optimism spoke 
0x6f26bf09b1c792e3228e5467807a900a503c0281, and the destination is its HubPool 
0xc186fa914353c44b2e33ebe05f21846f1048beda.
The trace and receipt show transferFrom releasing the exact DAI amount from local escrow to HubPool,
returning true and emitting Transfer. This route delivers an existing usable pool token despite differing
source/destination addresses. It releases escrow; it does not mint DAI.
These successful relays strengthen the destination-integration evidence. They also explain how postfork
withdrawals coexist with the earlier finding of no new selected StateCommitmentChain batches: the
supplied proofs were inherited. They do not prove that a newly asserted private-L2 balance has an
accepted fresh destination commitment. Existing unspent claims are finite.
The Across ownership proposal did execute through UMA governance
The June proposal and 19 June execution share both:
Proposal hash 0xcfcabb729c0274e198ef3ab0556577c135c587f95ee22403a408ab0e1ec9b766.• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 312

Assertion ID 0xbc640aecfd6f681d85bc31e7a12abcfd156f20616f6d96cdf8ae871e85f8fe54.
The proposal asks HubPool to transfer ownership from the Across Safe to feca. Its recorded challenge
interval is 432,000 seconds, five days, ending 19 June 2026 at 05:44:35 UTC. Execution follows at
05:46:05 UTC. The settlement event reports undisputed and truthful; the Safe module successfully
calls HubPool and its ownership event records feca as new owner.
Proposal + bond → UMA assertion → five-day challenge interval
                                      ↓ undisputed settlement
                              Across Safe module executes
                                      ↓
                               HubPool owner becomes feca
There is a material conflict between the embedded rules and the executed action: the rules say “oSnap
should not be used to call the HubPool contract”, yet HubPool is the target. They also require a
unique approved proposal identifier; the recorded explanation is just osnap. The receipts establish on-
chain acceptance and execution, not a valid off-chain Snapshot vote or compliance with those stated
rules. The verified implementation submits a claim to the oracle rather than parsing the governance
rules as an on-chain target allowlist. It permits proposal submission externally, subject to its bond and
oracle/escalation settings.
The current module's liveness getter is 1,200,000 seconds, and its collateral getter identifies the
copied UMA token. Those are later settings, not the five-day period and copied-WETH bond used in this
proposal. The earlier Across control audit (Appendix 3) separately proves that e121 acquired module
ownership on 19 August 2026. UMA's optimistic assertion system and Optimism's rollup messenger are
different systems.
The July owner-only call registers chain ID 88888, adapter 0x3233f8c0db384a2a1d6a307de41a804dfe411eb6, and
spoke 0x5c7bcd6e7de5423a257d81b442095a1a6ced35c5. The current getter matches. The sampled adapter source
and spoke implementation are unverified; this study does not establish that 88888 is the private pARB
network or that this configuration delivers fresh synths. The adapter's runtime cannot be treated as a
standard bridge solely from its configured address.
The June emergency deletion returns a bundle bond to 0xf7bac63fc7ceacf0589f25454ecf5c2ce904997c. It is
distinct from deleting an UMA governance proposal. BAD9's October 2024 fee deposit demonstrates
funding of HubPool, not a cross-chain transaction in that receipt.
Consequence for the thesis and reproduction
Confirmed Across authority can support route configuration and treasury operations. Inherited Optimism
claims can provide local inventory. Synthetix's separate owner relay supplies a credible administrative
architecture, and its native synth bridge has a distinct issuer-specific destination mint path. A functioning
new financing loop still needs accepted fresh source messages, exact usable outputs and destination
liquidity; Across ownership does not grant Synthetix mint permissions.
Raw records, source responses, failures and derived results are in artifacts/pulsechain-optimism-relay-
votes-20261001/. The explicit batch is Research/experiments/pulsechain_optimism_relay_transactions_20261001.json.
Reproduce its eight-transaction decode with:
python Research/scripts/analyze_pulsechain_optimism_relays.py Research/experiments/
pulsechain_optimism_relay_transactions_20261001.json --output /tmp/optimism-transaction-analysis.json
• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 313

The output path must be fresh. The command is offline. Current getter checkpoints are blocks 
27,684,339 and 27,684,371, with hashes retained in their raw records. Earlier ownership execution
records remain under artifacts/parb-across-control-20260929/; proposal-execution-match.json verifies the
matching event identifiers and records the rules conflict. No privileged action was performed or
simulated.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 314
